newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Dummy grenade hurled at Paraguayan armed forces HQ.
newsitem.headline: Dummy grenade hurled at Paraguayan armed forces HQ.

text.p: A small grenade thrown from a passing vehicle exploded on Tuesday night inside Paraguay's armed forces headquarters, authorities said on Wednesday.
There were no injuries and officials said the grenade may have been a plastic device used for military training.
"It was a small grenade without splinters that only explodes once," police inspector Pablo Marin, in charge of ballistic tests, said.

Government spokesmen said it was unclear whether the incident was an attack or a prank. President Juan Carlos Wasmosy, who is commander in chief of the armed forces, usually works at the military headquarters on Wednesdays.
The incident, just yards (metres) from Wasmosy's residence, occurred 10 days after unidentified assailants fired at the barracks of the presidential military guard.
The government did not immediately blame anyone for the attack, although Wasmosy said he suspected followers of former army chief Gen. Lino Oviedo.
"They are provoking us and waiting for our reaction in order to say later they are victims of government persecution," Wasmosy said.

Oviedo was forced to retire by Wasmosy after incidents last year that triggered fears of a military coup. Oviedo, holed up in his barracks in defiance of Wasmosy's orders that he be discharged, was later cleared in court of attempted rebellion. Oviedo, a sworn enemy of Wasmosy, is currently a presidential hopeful of the ruling Colorado Party.
